name: Arabian Sea
genZNote: The Arabian Sea is basically India's west-coast front door — Mumbai, Gujarat's ports, and the entire Gulf oil trade all funnel through it.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Ocean Connection
bullets: A north-western arm of the Indian Ocean, bounded by India to the east, Pakistan and Iran to the north, and the Arabian Peninsula to the west.
Connects to the Gulf of Aden (and onward to the Red Sea via Bab-el-Mandeb) in the northwest, and to the Persian Gulf via the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries Bordering It
bullets: India (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala coastlines), Pakistan, Iran (partly, via the Gulf of Oman approach), Oman, Yemen, and the Maldives lie within or near it.
Somalia's coastline is often grouped with the wider Arabian Sea/Indian Ocean region for trade purposes.

sections.heading: 🚢 Ports & Trade Routes
bullets: Major ports: Mumbai (Jawaharlal Nehru Port/JNPT) and Mundra/Kandla in Gujarat on the Indian side; Karachi and Gwadar in Pakistan; Salalah in Oman.
Carries the bulk of India's crude oil imports from the Gulf, along with container trade to East Africa and the Gulf states.
The route from the Gulf to India across the Arabian Sea is one of the busiest energy-trade corridors in the world.

sections.heading: 🐠 Economic & Ecological Significance
bullets: Supports major fisheries along India's west coast, particularly for mackerel, sardines and shrimp.
Monsoon-driven upwelling brings nutrient-rich water to the surface, supporting these fisheries seasonally.
Increasingly studied for oxygen-minimum-zone expansion, a marine ecological concern linked to warming waters.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Arabian Sea is a north-western arm of the Indian Ocean between India, Pakistan, Iran and the Arabian Peninsula, central to India's western trade and energy imports.
keyFacts: Part of the Indian Ocean; borders India's west coast, Pakistan, Iran, Oman, Yemen.
Connects onward to the Persian Gulf (via Hormuz) and the Red Sea (via Bab-el-Mandeb/Gulf of Aden).
Major Indian ports: JNPT (Mumbai), Mundra, Kandla.
commonConfusion: The Arabian Sea is a sea, not the Persian Gulf — the Gulf is a separate, smaller body reached via the Strait of Hormuz.

highYieldFacts: Arabian Sea = NW arm of the Indian Ocean; India's west coast, Pakistan, Iran, Arabian Peninsula.
JNPT (Mumbai) is India's busiest container port on this coast.
Connects to the Persian Gulf via the Strait of Hormuz.
commonTraps: Don't call it the same body of water as the Persian Gulf — they connect but are distinct.
mustRemember: Arabian Sea = India's west-coast energy and trade gateway to the Gulf.

sources.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Government of India
